question: Which class consists of misfolded proteins that transmit their abnormal conformation to normal variants of the same protein?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the classes of human pathogens/pathogenic microbes

options.rationale: Prions propagate by transmitting an abnormal protein conformation to normal variants of the same protein.
Viruses produce cytopathic or cytoproliferative effects in host cells. Viral inclusion bodies or host-cell changes would support this choice.
Bacteria are living prokaryotic microorganisms rather than transmissible misfolded proteins. Bacterial morphology or culture growth would support this choice.
Fungi are nucleated eukaryotes with thick cell walls. Hyphae, budding yeasts, or dimorphism would support this choice.
Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotic organisms that may replicate intracellularly or extracellularly. Microscopic trophozoites or cysts would support this choice.

question: A tissue section contains a dense collection of cells whose granule product includes major basic protein. Which pathogen category most characteristically produces this response?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Pyogenic bacteria characteristically recruit neutrophils. A purulent infiltrate with myeloperoxidase-containing cells would support this choice.
Parasitic metazoan infections characteristically produce eosinophilic inflammation, and eosinophil major basic protein is toxic to parasites.
Viral infections generally produce mononuclear or cytopathic patterns rather than a major basic protein-rich response. Inclusion bodies or cellular proliferation would support this choice.
Intracellular bacteria may provoke mononuclear inflammation. A lymphocytic or histiocytic infiltrate would support this choice.
Fungi may produce suppurative or granulomatous inflammation. Hyphae or budding yeasts with those patterns would support this choice.

question: Which staining method is most specifically associated with demonstrating the capsule of Cryptococcus species?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Ziehl-Neelsen staining is used for mycobacteria. Acid-fast organisms would make this method appropriate.
Giemsa staining can identify Campylobacter, Leishmania, and malaria parasites. One of those organisms would support this method.
Mucicarmine demonstrates the capsule of Cryptococcus species and supports identification of encapsulated budding yeast.
Gram staining is primarily used to identify most bacteria. A suspected bacterial infection would support this method.
GMS staining can demonstrate fungi but is not the capsule-specific method presented for Cryptococcus. Broad fungal visualization would support this choice.

question: Which fungal morphology is characteristic of Rhizopus and Mucor species?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the classes of human pathogens/pathogenic microbes

options.rationale: Septate hyphae with acute-angle branching characterize Aspergillus species. That branching pattern would make this choice correct.
Large broad-based budding yeasts characterize Blastomyces dermatitidis. Budding rather than hyphal growth would support this choice.
Narrow-based budding occurs in several yeast-form fungi. Rounded budding organisms rather than broad hyphae would support this choice.
Rhizopus and Mucor have wide, pauci-septate hyphae with approximately 90-degree branching.
Large spherules containing endospores characterize Coccidioides immitis. Spherules rather than branching hyphae would support this choice.

question: A pathogen resists eradication and produces a compact aggregate of activated phagocytic cells, some of which fuse. Which inflammatory pattern is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Identify/describe histological patterns of tissue reaction in infections

options.rationale: Suppurative inflammation features vascular leakage and neutrophil-rich pus. Abundant neutrophils responding to pyogenic bacteria would support this choice.
Eosinophilic inflammation is associated with metazoan parasites. Eosinophils containing major basic protein would support this choice.
Cytoproliferative reactions involve rapid host-cell proliferation, often caused by viruses. Papules or warts would support this choice.
Toxin-mediated necrosis causes rapid tissue destruction and may have minimal inflammation. Extensive necrosis without organized phagocyte aggregates would support this choice.
Granulomatous inflammation is a distinctive mononuclear pattern formed by tight macrophage aggregates that may fuse into multinucleated giant cells.

question: A tissue sample shows abundant neutrophils responding to extracellular cocci. Which neutrophil product contributes directly to killing and degradation of engulfed organisms?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the pathological patterns and spectrum of inflammatory responses produced by different pathogens

options.rationale: Myeloperoxidase is a functional neutrophil product involved in killing and degrading engulfed pathogens.
Major basic protein is an eosinophil product toxic to parasites. A metazoan infection with eosinophilic inflammation would support this choice.
A mucicarmine-positive capsule is a structural feature of Cryptococcus rather than a neutrophil product. Encapsulated budding yeast would support this finding.
Misfolded protein aggregates are associated with prion propagation rather than neutrophil killing. Spongiform neuronal injury would support this choice.
Viral inclusion bodies are aggregates associated with viral particles or effects in host cells. Cytopathic cellular changes would support this finding.

question: A specimen obtained during the early stage of a suspected infection is tested serologically. Which result provides the most direct evidence of recent onset?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: An unchanged convalescent titer does not meet the diagnostic serologic criterion. A fourfold interval increase would support recent infection.
Detection of specific IgM shortly after symptom onset provides serologic evidence of a recent infection.
A nonspecific single titer lacks the specificity and temporal pattern described for diagnosis. Pathogen-specific IgM or paired titers would support infection.
A twofold rise is below the stated diagnostic threshold. A fourfold rise between acute and convalescent samples would make this approach diagnostic.
Absence of an acute antibody response does not provide positive serologic evidence of recent infection. Specific IgM would support this conclusion.

question: A pathologist compares serum collected at presentation with serum collected five weeks later. Which change satisfies the stated diagnostic criterion?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: An unchanged titer does not demonstrate the interval rise required for diagnosis. A fourfold rise would satisfy the criterion.
A twofold increase is below the stated diagnostic threshold. A fourfold increase would make this choice correct.
A fourfold rise between acute and convalescent titers obtained 4-6 weeks apart is considered diagnostic.
A decline does not meet the stated rising-titer criterion. A fourfold increase would support diagnosis.
Absent convalescent antibody does not demonstrate the required immune response. A fourfold titer rise would support recent infection.

question: A chronic infection produces an infiltrate dominated by plasma cells rather than lymphocytes or macrophages. Which infectious category best matches this cellular pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Hepatitis B characteristically produces lymphocyte-predominant mononuclear inflammation. Lymphocytic predominance would make this choice correct.
Mycobacterial infections characteristically produce macrophage or histiocyte predominance. Tight macrophage aggregates would support this choice.
Pyogenic bacterial infections usually produce neutrophilic inflammation. Pus formation with abundant neutrophils would support this choice.
Syphilis is associated with plasma cell-predominant mononuclear inflammation, as is Lyme disease.
Metazoan infections generally produce eosinophilic inflammation. Eosinophils with major basic protein would support this choice.

question: A viral process causes rapid turnover and expansion of infected epithelial cells rather than predominantly killing them. Which tissue reaction best describes this effect?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the pathological patterns and spectrum of inflammatory responses produced by different pathogens

options.rationale: Suppurative reactions are neutrophil-rich responses generally associated with pyogenic bacteria. Pus formation would support this choice.
Eosinophilic reactions are associated with metazoan parasites. Parasite-toxic eosinophil products would support this choice.
Granulomatous reactions contain compact macrophage accumulations responding to agents that resist eradication. Giant cells would support this choice.
Cytopathic effects produce apoptosis or necrosis rather than the emphasized cellular expansion. Blisters or ulcers from cell death would support this choice.
Cytoproliferative viral effects cause rapid cellular turnover and proliferation, producing lesions such as papules or warts.

question: A fungal isolate changes between filamentous and rounded budding forms according to environmental temperature. Which classification best describes the organism?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the classes of human pathogens/pathogenic microbes

options.rationale: Dimorphic fungi exist as molds or yeasts depending on environmental conditions and temperature.
A septate mold is defined by divided hyphae rather than temperature-dependent conversion to yeast. Persistent septate hyphae would support this choice.
A pauci-septate mold has broad hyphae with few septa rather than two temperature-dependent forms. Right-angle branching hyphae would support this choice.
An encapsulated yeast is identified by a capsule, such as the mucicarmine-positive capsule of Cryptococcus. Capsule demonstration would support this choice.
A yeast form reproduces mainly by budding but does not explain conversion to a mold form. Growth exclusively as rounded budding cells would support this choice.

question: A brain biopsy contains porous-appearing parenchyma and neuronal injury without evidence of a living microorganism. Which pathogenic process best explains these findings?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the classes of human pathogens/pathogenic microbes

options.rationale: Viral injury may produce cellular inclusions, necrosis, or proliferation. Viral host-cell changes would support this choice.
Prions transmit an abnormal protein conformation and produce neuronal damage with distinctive spongiform change.
Bacterial toxins can cause rapid necrosis but do not define transmissible spongiform encephalopathy. Severe tissue necrosis with minimal inflammation would support this choice.
Fungal invasion would be supported by visible hyphae or yeasts. Those forms are absent from the described process.
Protozoal disease may cause necrosis and can show visible organisms. Trophozoites or cysts would support this choice.

question: A microbiology laboratory needs a single method capable of identifying genetic material from any major pathogen class. Which technique best fulfills this requirement?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Gram staining is primarily used for most bacteria and does not identify all pathogen classes. Suspected bacterial morphology would support this choice.
Acid-fast staining is used for mycobacteria and modified staining for Nocardia. Those organisms would support this choice.
DNA probes and PCR are listed as identification techniques applicable to all pathogen classes.
Mucicarmine is used for Cryptococcus species rather than all pathogen classes. An encapsulated yeast would support this choice.
Giemsa staining identifies selected bacteria and parasites rather than every pathogen class. Malaria parasites or Leishmania would support this choice.

question: A viral inclusion appears as an eosinophilic cytoplasmic body within a cerebellar Purkinje cell. Which named structure is most consistent with this finding?
cited_learning_objective: Identify/describe histological patterns of tissue reaction in infections

options.rationale: Cowdry type A bodies are intranuclear droplet-like inclusions with a clear halo. An intranuclear herpesvirus-associated inclusion would support this choice.
Henderson-Paterson bodies are large eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in molluscum contagiosum lesions. Epidermal proliferation would support this choice.
Warthin-Finkeldey cells are multinucleated cells containing nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions in measles. That combined distribution would support this choice.
Negri bodies are eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions found in Purkinje cells in rabies.
Owl's-eye inclusions are intranuclear findings associated with cytomegalovirus. An enlarged cell with a prominent nuclear inclusion would support this choice.

question: An organism grows as septate filaments that branch at acute angles. Histologic examination cannot distinguish among several species within its genus. Which additional procedure is needed for identification?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Paired serology assesses an antibody response and does not provide the stated method for distinguishing these histologically identical molds. A fourfold titer rise would support recent infection.
Mucicarmine demonstrates the capsule of Cryptococcus rather than distinguishing septate molds. Encapsulated budding yeast would support this choice.
Modified acid-fast staining is associated with Nocardia rather than species identification of acute-angle branching fungi. Suspected Nocardia would support this choice.
A wet mount may demonstrate fungal material but does not resolve the stated species-level limitation of identical histology. A basic need to visualize fungi could support this choice.
Aspergillus species look alike histologically, so culture and microbiologic assessment are needed for species identification.

question: A 41-year-old man develops a rapidly enlarging area of tissue destruction. Biopsy shows extensive necrosis with surprisingly little inflammatory infiltrate. Which mechanism most likely produced this pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Powerful toxins produced by organisms such as Clostridium perfringens can cause rapid, severe necrosis with minimal inflammation.
Eosinophil granules participate in responses to metazoan parasites rather than producing the characteristic toxin-mediated necrosis. Eosinophil-rich inflammation would support this choice.
Granuloma formation produces organized macrophage aggregates in response to persistent agents. Tight aggregates and giant cells would support this choice.
Viral cytoproliferative effects cause rapid cellular turnover and lesions such as papules or warts. Cellular expansion rather than severe necrosis would support this choice.
Fibrosis develops after chronic inflammation and repeated injury rather than causing rapid tissue destruction. Extensive scarring would support this choice.

question: A 28-year-old woman has multiple small, waxy skin papules with central depressions. Biopsy shows epidermal proliferation containing large eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. Which diagnosis is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Rabies produces Negri bodies in Purkinje cells rather than proliferative umbilicated papules. Cytoplasmic inclusions in cerebellar neurons would support this choice.
Molluscum contagiosum produces centrally umbilicated waxy papules with Henderson-Paterson bodies in proliferating epidermis.
Cytomegalovirus produces prominent intranuclear owl's-eye inclusions. Enlarged cells containing nuclear inclusions would support this choice.
Herpes simplex produces multinucleation, margination, and molding rather than Henderson-Paterson bodies. Those three nuclear effects would support this choice.
Adenovirus produces intranuclear inclusions and may cause conjunctival, respiratory, intestinal, or bladder disease. Nuclear inclusions in those settings would support this choice.

question: A 36-year-old patient has an ulcerated lesion. Infected cells demonstrate multinucleation, peripheral displacement of chromatin, and nuclei conforming to one another. Which pathogen group most likely caused these changes?
cited_learning_objective: Identify/describe histological patterns of tissue reaction in infections

options.rationale: Poxviruses can produce cytoplasmic inclusions, including Henderson-Paterson or Guarnieri bodies. Cytoplasmic inclusions would support this choice.
Adenoviruses produce intranuclear inclusions but not the described triad. Conjunctivitis or hemorrhagic cystitis with nuclear inclusions would support this choice.
Multinucleation, chromatin margination, and nuclear molding are the characteristic three viral effects associated with herpes simplex virus.
Rabies produces eosinophilic cytoplasmic Negri bodies in Purkinje cells. That neuronal finding would support this choice.
Measles produces Warthin-Finkeldey cells with nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions. Those multinucleated cells in the characteristic clinical setting would support this choice.

question: A 24-year-old patient has cough, nasal discharge, conjunctival inflammation, oral mucosal spots, and a rash. Tissue contains large multinucleated cells with inclusions in two cellular compartments. Which finding is expected?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Negri bodies are cytoplasmic inclusions in Purkinje cells associated with rabies. Cerebellar involvement with those inclusions would support this choice.
Owl's-eye inclusions are intranuclear changes associated with cytomegalovirus. A TORCH infection, retinitis, or encephalitis would support this choice.
Cowdry type A bodies are intranuclear droplet-like masses with clear halos in herpesvirus infections. A herpesvirus cytopathic pattern would support this choice.
The clinical pattern and multinucleated cells containing both nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions identify Warthin-Finkeldey cells.
Henderson-Paterson bodies occur in molluscum contagiosum within proliferating epidermis. Umbilicated waxy papules would support this choice.

question: A 52-year-old bird handler develops disease involving the lungs and central nervous system. Tissue shows 4-8 µm narrow-based budding organisms surrounded by clear halos. Which stain is the best next diagnostic step?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Ziehl-Neelsen staining identifies mycobacteria rather than an encapsulated budding yeast. Suspected mycobacterial disease would support this choice.
Giemsa staining is used for Campylobacter, Leishmania, and malaria parasites. One of those infectious settings would support this choice.
Gram staining is primarily used for most bacteria. A bacterial morphology question would support this choice.
Periodic acid-Schiff can demonstrate fungi but does not specifically highlight the defining capsule. General fungal visualization without a capsule question would support this choice.
The morphology and organ distribution indicate Cryptococcus, whose capsule is demonstrated with mucicarmine.

question: A 47-year-old patient from a wet river-valley region has pulmonary and cutaneous disease. Tissue shows 8-20 µm yeast cells with broad attachment sites between parent and bud. Which organism is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Blastomyces occurs in wet regions, involves lungs and skin, and forms large broad-based budding yeasts.
Coccidioides occurs in desert regions and forms large spherules containing endospores. That environmental and tissue morphology combination would support this choice.
Cryptococcus forms medium narrow-based budding yeasts with mucicarmine-positive capsules. A clear halo and pigeon exposure would support this choice.
Histoplasma forms small 1-5 µm narrow-based budding yeasts. Small organisms associated with bird or bat excrement would support this choice.
Sporothrix forms small oval narrow-based budding yeasts and involves skin and lymphatic vessels. Plant exposure with lymphatic spread would support this choice.

question: A 39-year-old patient who handled plant material develops lesions extending from the skin along lymphatic vessels. Tissue contains small oval narrow-based budding yeasts. Which organism is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Blastomyces produces larger broad-based budding yeasts and commonly affects the lungs and skin. That morphology and pulmonary involvement would support this choice.
Sporothrix is associated with plant material, involves skin and lymphatics, and forms small oval narrow-based budding yeasts.
Coccidioides forms spherules containing endospores and is associated with desert exposure. Those findings would support this choice.
Cryptococcus forms encapsulated narrow-based budding yeasts and may involve lungs, brain, eye, skin, or nasal cavity. A mucicarmine-positive capsule would support this choice.
Histoplasma is associated with bird and bat excrement in wet regions and primarily begins in the lungs. That exposure and distribution would support this choice.

question: A 31-year-old traveler from a desert region develops pulmonary disease that later involves bone and skin. Tissue contains large structures filled with numerous smaller internal forms. Which organism is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Blastomyces forms broad-based budding yeast cells rather than endospore-filled spherules. Wet-region exposure with broad-based buds would support this choice.
Cryptococcus forms encapsulated narrow-based budding yeasts associated with pigeon excrement. A mucicarmine-positive capsule would support this choice.
Coccidioides is associated with desert regions and forms large spherules containing numerous small endospores.
Histoplasma forms small narrow-based budding yeast cells rather than large spherules. Bird or bat exposure in a wet region would support this choice.
Sporothrix causes cutaneous and lymphatic disease after plant exposure and forms small oval budding yeasts. That pattern would support this choice.

question: A 44-year-old patient from a wet region reports substantial exposure to bird and bat excrement. Pulmonary infection disseminates to other organs, and tissue contains 1-5 µm narrow-based budding cells. Which organism is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Blastomyces forms larger 8-20 µm broad-based budding yeasts. Large broad-based buds would support this choice.
Coccidioides is associated with desert regions and forms spherules containing endospores. Those findings would support this choice.
Cryptococcus forms 4-8 µm encapsulated narrow-based budding yeasts and is associated with pigeon excrement. A mucicarmine-positive capsule would support this choice.
Histoplasma is associated with bird and bat excrement in wet regions and forms small narrow-based budding yeasts.
Sporothrix is associated with plant material and spreads along lymphatic vessels. A cutaneous lymphatic pattern would support this choice.

question: A 34-year-old patient develops bloody intestinal disease complicated by a hepatic abscess. Colonic biopsy shows deep ulcers with a narrow surface opening and numerous motile forms. Which diagnostic finding is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Entamoeba histolytica produces flask-shaped ulcers and may be identified by trophozoites or cysts in stool.
Sporozoites and oocysts belong to the described Toxoplasma life cycle rather than amebic intestinal disease. Toxoplasma exposure or dissemination would support this choice.

Taenia solium is identified through eggs or proglottids in an intestinal infection, but the stated specimen is not urine and the ulcer pattern is amebic. Tapeworm segments would support that diagnosis.
Hyphae and yeasts indicate fungal infection rather than Entamoeba-associated flask-shaped ulcers. Fungal morphology would support this choice.
Hydatid sand contains protoscolices and brood capsules in Echinococcus cysts. A gross tissue cyst with those contents would support this choice.

question: A 29-year-old pregnant patient acquires a protozoal infection that can cross the placenta during its disseminating acute phase. Which organism form mediates this transmission?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the classes of human pathogens/pathogenic microbes

options.rationale: Bradyzoites are dormant tissue forms associated with chronic infection. Chronic tissue persistence rather than acute transplacental spread would support this choice.
Tachyzoites disseminate during acute Toxoplasma infection and can be transmitted transplacentally.
Oocysts are ingested by intermediate hosts and release sporozoites in the intestine. Environmental acquisition rather than placental transmission would support this choice.
Sporozoites emerge from ingested oocysts and penetrate intestinal epithelium before differentiating. Initial intestinal invasion would support this choice.
Brood capsules are associated with Echinococcus hydatid cysts rather than Toxoplasma transmission. A hydatid cyst containing protoscolices would support this choice.

question: A 46-year-old patient develops central nervous system lesions after fecal-oral exposure to eggs from a pork tapeworm. Which disease process best explains the tissue involvement?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Intestinal taeniasis follows ingestion of cysts in raw or undercooked pork. That route with disease confined to the intestine would support this choice.
Cystic echinococcosis follows ingestion of Echinococcus eggs and produces hydatid cysts. Hydatid sand would support this choice.
Fecal-oral ingestion of Taenia solium eggs produces tissue infection, including neurocysticercosis.
Entamoeba histolytica produces amebic dysentery and flask-shaped intestinal ulcers. Trophozoites in colonic ulcers would support this choice.
Toxoplasma dissemination follows liberation of sporozoites and development of tachyzoites, not pork tapeworm eggs. Tachyzoite dissemination would support this choice.

question: A 50-year-old patient has a large visceral cyst acquired after fecal-oral ingestion of helminth eggs. Aspirated material contains free-floating immature tapeworm structures with hooklets. Which finding names this material?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Henderson-Paterson bodies are viral cytoplasmic inclusions in molluscum contagiosum. Umbilicated papules with epidermal proliferation would support this choice.
Warthin-Finkeldey cells are multinucleated viral cells containing nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions. Measles-associated findings would support this choice.
Cowdry type A bodies are intranuclear viral inclusions with clear halos. Herpesvirus infection would support this choice.
Hydatid sand contains free-floating protoscolices with hooklets and brood capsules within Echinococcus cysts.
Negri bodies are eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in Purkinje cells. Rabies involving the central nervous system would support this choice.

question: A 63-year-old immunocompromised patient develops disseminated disease after environmental fungal exposure. Which host factor most directly fits a recognized predisposition to opportunistic mycosis?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Indwelling catheters and prosthetic devices predispose to opportunistic fungal infection, but they are not specified in this patient. Device-associated infection would make this choice correct.
Antibiotic therapy is a recognized fungal risk factor, but no antibiotic exposure is provided. Recent broad antimicrobial use would support this choice.
High glucose content predisposes to opportunistic fungal infection, but no glucose abnormality is given. Documented high glucose would support this choice.
Debilitation is a recognized fungal risk factor, but the decisive host condition stated here is impaired immunity. A debilitated immunocompetent host would support this choice.
Immunocompromise or immunosuppression is a major recognized predisposition to opportunistic fungal disease and dissemination.

question: A 58-year-old patient has a bacterial abscess sampled early in its evolution. A repeat specimen several days later shows a changing cellular composition. Which sequence is most expected?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the pathological patterns and spectrum of inflammatory responses produced by different pathogens

options.rationale: Bacterial infections usually begin with a neutrophilic response and develop increasing macrophages and lymphocytes over time.
Eosinophils are associated with parasitic metazoan infection rather than the later phase of a typical bacterial response. Helminth infection would support this sequence.
Plasma cells are associated with selected mononuclear responses, while neutrophils predominate early in bacterial infection. A later-to-earlier reversal is not expected here.
This sequence does not match the described evolution of bacterial inflammation. Viral inflammation followed by a metazoan response would be required to support it.
Eosinophils and plasma cells correspond to different infectious response patterns rather than the usual bacterial sequence. A parasitic process followed by a plasma cell-rich process would be needed.

question: A 37-year-old patient has an infection in which the organism is not visible by light microscopy, but infected cells contain stainable aggregates in the nucleus. Which pathogen class is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Identify/describe histological patterns of tissue reaction in infections

options.rationale: Prions produce spongiform neuronal injury through protein misfolding rather than intracellular inclusion bodies. Porous brain change would support this choice.
Viruses cannot be seen by light microscopy, but their inclusion bodies can appear as stainable nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates.
Bacteria are living prokaryotes commonly evaluated by stains, shape, culture, and biochemical testing. Visible bacterial forms would support this choice.
Fungi can be seen by light microscopy as hyphae or rounded yeasts. Those visible forms would support this choice.
Metazoa are multicellular eukaryotic organisms and may be visible to the naked eye. Worms or ectoparasites would support this choice.

question: A 45-year-old patient has chronic pulmonary infection. Biopsy shows organized macrophage aggregates with multinucleated giant cells and associated lymphocytes. Which microbial property most directly accounts for this pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Understand the pathological patterns and spectrum of inflammatory responses produced by different pathogens

options.rationale: Powerful extracellular toxins produce rapid necrosis with potentially minimal inflammation. Extensive acute tissue destruction would support this choice.
Neutrophil chemoattraction produces suppurative inflammation associated with pyogenic bacteria. Pus and abundant neutrophils would support this choice.
Agents that resist eradication provoke granulomatous inflammation with compact macrophage aggregates and possible giant-cell formation.

Temperature-dependent conversion defines fungal dimorphism but does not itself explain the organized macrophage response. Demonstration of mold and yeast forms under different conditions would support this choice.
Rapid epithelial proliferation is a cytoproliferative viral effect. Papules or warts with sparse inflammation would support this choice.

question: A 33-year-old patient develops severe brain injury marked by necrosis and hemorrhage with only a small inflammatory response. Which organism best matches this pathological pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Associate tissue reaction pattern with types of pathogens that may be responsible for the infection

options.rationale: Entamoeba histolytica causes intestinal flask-shaped ulcers and may produce liver abscesses. Amebic dysentery with trophozoites would support this choice.

Toxoplasma can disseminate in immunocompromised hosts, but the specified hemorrhagic brain necrosis with minimal inflammation is assigned to another protozoan. Tachyzoites or bradyzoite cysts would support this choice.
Trichomonas affects the urogenital system and is identified by Pap testing or wet preparation. Urogenital infection would support this choice.
Naegleria fowleri causes substantial brain necrosis and hemorrhage with minimal inflammation.
Plasmodium species are blood-associated protozoa identified with Giemsa staining. Blood parasites on a stained specimen would support this choice.

question: A 26-year-old patient has a suspected urogenital protozoal infection. Which initial specimen-based method is most appropriate for direct identification?
cited_learning_objective: Review approach to pathological diagnosis, mechanisms of microbial injury, and techniques for identifying infectious agents

options.rationale: Acid-fast staining targets mycobacteria and modified staining can identify Nocardia. Suspected infection with those bacteria would support this choice.
Mucicarmine demonstrates the capsule of Cryptococcus species. Encapsulated budding yeast would support this choice.

Paired titers can diagnose infection through a fourfold rise but are not the direct identification methods presented for this urogenital protozoan. An infection requiring serologic confirmation would support this choice.
Gross cyst and aspirate examination are used for Echinococcus hydatid disease. A visceral cyst containing hydatid sand would support this choice.
Trichomonas vaginalis affects the urogenital system and is identified using a Pap specimen or wet preparation.
